<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par107" />willed), or as in some way conditional, and consequently only contingent. More particularly such imperfects serve—

{{GHGmargin-letter|107|n}}
(''a'') As an expression of will, whether it be a definite intention and arrangement, or a simple desire, viz.:

(1) Sometimes in positive sentences in place of the cohortative (cf. e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=59|verse=17}} with verse 18; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=22|verse=50}} with {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=50}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=19|verse=11}}, &c.), of the imperative ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=18|verse=3}}), or of the jussive (which, however, in most cases, does not differ from the ordinary form of the imperfect), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תֵּֽרָאֶה|translate=let it appear}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=34|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=19|verse=2}}, 3, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=10|verse=12}} (and so frequently in verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}; cf. {{GHGpar|109|a}}, note 2); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=9|verse=5}} ({{GHGheb|text=תָּחִיל}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=61|verse=7}} ({{GHGheb|text=תּוֹסִיף}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=22|verse=17}} ({{GHGheb|text=תָּשִׁית}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=23|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=6|verse=23}} (co-ordinated with the imperative), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=10|verse=20|hidebook=1}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}; so probably also {{GHGheb|text=יָדִין|translate=let him judge!}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=72|verse=2}}.—So also in the 1st pers., to express a wish which is asserted subsequently with reference to a fixed point of time in the past, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=10|verse=18}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶגְּוַע|translate=I ought to}} [not ''should'' as A.V., R.V.] ''have'', (then, immediately after being born) ''given up the ghost''; cf. verse 19 {{GHGheb|text=אֶֽהְיֶה}} and {{GHGheb|text=אוּבָֽל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=10|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=35|verse=28}}. Even to express an obligation or necessity according to the judgement of another person, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=9|verse=29}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶרְשָׁע|translate=I am to be guilty}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=12|verse=4|hidebook=1}}. Cp. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=9|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=16|hidebook=1}}; in a question, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=42|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=43|verse=2|hidebook=1}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|107|o}}
(2) To express the definite expectation that something will not happen. The imperfect with {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} represents a more emphatic form of prohibition than the jussive<ref>As stated in {{GHGpar|46|a}}, a prohibition cannot be expressed by {{GHGheb|text=אַל־}} and the imperative.</ref> with {{GHGheb|text=אַל־}} (cf. {{GHGpar|109|c}}), and corresponds to our ''thou shalt not do it!'' with the strongest expectation of obedience, while {{GHGheb|text=אַל־}} with the jussive is rather a simple warning, ''do not that!'' Thus {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} with the imperfect is especially used in enforcing the divine commands, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=לֹא תִּגְנֹב|translate=thou shalt not steal}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=20|verse=15}}; cf. verses 3, 4, 5, 7, 10 ff. So {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} with the 3rd pers. perhaps in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=16|verse=10}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|107|p}}
Rem. The {{GHGterm|jussive}}, which is to be expected after {{GHGheb|text=אַל־}}, does not, as a rule (according to ''n'', and {{GHGpar|109|a}}, note 2), differ in form from the simple imperfect. That many supposed jussives are intended as simple imperfects is possible from the occurrence after {{GHGheb|text=אַל־}} of what are undoubtedly imperfect forms, not only from verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} (cf. {{GHGpar|109|a}}, note 2), but also from verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}, to express a prohibition or negative wish, {{GHGheb|text=אַל־תַּבִּיט}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=17}}, {{GHGheb|text=אַל־תָּסוּר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=1|verse=7}}, {{GHGheb|text=אַל־נָא יָשִׂים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=25}}. Even with the 1st pers. plur. (after an imperative) {{GHGheb|text=וְאַל־נָמוּת|translate=that we die not}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=12|verse=19}}. Also to express the conviction that something cannot happen, {{GHGheb|text=אַל־יָנוּם|translate=he will not slumber}},<ref>To regard this as an optative (so Hupfeld) is from the context impossible. It is more probably a strong pregnant construction, or fusion of two sentences (such as, ''do not think he will slumber!''). Verse 4 contains the objective confirmation, by means of {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} with the imperf., of that which was previously only a subjective conviction.</ref> {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=121|verse=3}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=46|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=14|verse=10}}.<section end="par107" /><noinclude>
